policy_floor: non-RAII manual cleanup in NEW C++
trigger: Any failing Catch2 REQUIRE between sqlite3_open and sqlite3_close in the upgrade-path test - i.e. exactly the regression the test exists to catch
summary: Raw sqlite3*/sqlite3_stmt* with four throwing REQUIREs between acquire and release leaks the connection, and a live statement on one path. Found INDEPENDENTLY by cpp-safety and security-guardian in the same wave; both located the existing yuzu::test::SqliteHandleOwner / yuzu::server::SqliteStmt owners.
classification_rationale: A resource-ownership defect in code, not prose.

policy_floor: Resource Ledger omission on a C++ diff
trigger: Gate 1 Resource Ledger drafted against a4a44b20 asserted 'no new sqlite3*' while 01eae617 adds exactly that
summary: Resource Ledger became false when the test commit landed; corrected with a full owner/acquire/release/transfer/failure-cleanup table.
classification_rationale: A required governance artefact was incomplete; absence, not wording.

trigger: An integrator consults rest-api.md to learn which permission gates the three engine-principal reads after upgrading
summary: rest-api.md still documented Security:Read for the three moved routes; the OpenAPI JSON was updated but the human-readable permission call-outs were not. Senior found a fifth site in the same file's section intro that the reporter missed.
classification_rationale: Doc contradicts code on the authoritative per-endpoint permission contract.

trigger: A future contributor forks kTopologyFloor into a second floor list, or moves the check above rbac_enforcement_in_effect
summary: authz_topology_floor.hpp declared itself a single chokepoint in the dispatch_confined_arms family but had no routed-concern row, so per the policy-floor definition a future fork would NOT have gated. Found independently by architect and docs-writer.
classification_rationale: Six-item list, item 4: a new architectural invariant needs a CLAUDE.md line or routed-concern row.

trigger: Reading rbac.md's ITServiceOwner row to learn which securables it excludes
summary: ITServiceOwner 'Excludes' list named four of five excluded securables; AccessReview was missing. Pre-existing, but this change re-numbered the line.
classification_rationale: Enumeration contradicts itso_types[].

trigger: Reading the decision doc's route-keying rationale
summary: 'byte-identical perm_fn calls' immediately followed by a description of how their arguments differ; they are identically SHAPED on the same req.path.
classification_rationale: Wording only; filed by docs-writer as the sole owner of wording.

trigger: An operator reads mcp.md or audit-log.md to learn what to grant a custom role for the engine-principal tools
summary: The SAME stale-permission class round 1 fixed in rest-api.md survived in mcp.md (tool table + prose) and audit-log.md (engine_principal.role.listed gate). I6 raised to HIGH by FALSE ASSURANCE: following the doc grants a permission that no longer reaches the surface.
classification_rationale: Docs contradict kToolSecurityRows.

trigger: Operator revokes a seeded built-in-role grant (e.g. Viewer's EnginePrincipal:Read) and restarts the server
summary: seed_defaults() re-seeding unconditionally - the property the no-migration decision RESTS on - also means a deliberately revoked grant returns on next boot with no distinguishing audit line. Pre-existing across all 23 securables. Recorded in the decision doc because this change DEPENDS on the behaviour; durable fix is a tombstone mechanism across all seeding.
classification_rationale: A real behavioural defect, not prose.

trigger: A non-admin compliance evidence collector polls the access-review export after upgrade and treats non-2xx as 'no grants'
summary: The documented breaking change could silently break a CC6.2 evidence collector for a whole audit period. Folded: the upgrade note now names non-interactive readers explicitly and calls out the evidence-collector case.
classification_rationale: Six-item list, item 2: a required user-manual upgrade step was incomplete.

trigger: An assessor reads the SOC 2 evidence narrative for CC6.2 and sees no record of the pre-#2376 exposure
summary: The narrative cited role-assignment exports as clean CC6.2 evidence without recording that the export was readable by any authenticated user on a default install until this change. Addendum added in the doc's own established pattern.
classification_rationale: Compliance-evidence completeness; absence, not wording.

trigger: A reader takes access-reviews-2026-07-21.md's 'granted only to Administrator and Reviewer' as unconditional
summary: Claims were RBAC-on-scoped without saying so. Forward-pointer addendum added.
classification_rationale: Unqualified claim was false on the default posture.

trigger: unresolved
summary: Considered a boot-time scan warning when a custom role holds Security:Read but not EnginePrincipal:Read. The reporter recommended AGAINST it as disproportionate for a one-time single-securable cut already covered by the upgrade note and verifiable via GET /rbac/roles/{role}/permissions.
classification_rationale: A design option assessed and declined by the reporter itself.

trigger: Corrupt / mid-migration / locked rbac.db reaching the floor with an unexpected role
summary: Hypothesis that a corrupt store could reach the floor. Refuted by its own author during the same review.
classification_rationale: Claim tested and found false.
refuted_by: rbac_enforcement_in_effect() returns true whenever !is_open() (a failed migration sets db_=nullptr), which routes to check_permission on a dead handle - always false, always deny - so the legacy branch the floor lives in is never reached. Verified by reading rbac_store.cpp:770 and auth_routes.cpp:698/882.

trigger: An operator provisions a custom role from auth-architecture.md's REST-gating bullet for the engine-principal surface
summary: auth-architecture.md still documented the engine-principal reads as Security:Read, contradicting the section 250 lines earlier that this change added. FOURTH round of one defect class, and the senior's error: round 2's commit claimed a complete sweep of docs/, the line WAS in that sweep's output, and it was eyeballed past. Sweeping without auditing the results is not a sweep.
classification_rationale: File contradicts both the code and itself.

trigger: A future governance agent reads .claude/routed-concerns.md - @-imported into EVERY session - and enforces the wrong permission for /engine-principals/{id}/roles
summary: Found while doing the round-3 sweep properly: the same propagated sentence asserting Security:Read gates /engine-principals/{id}/roles appeared in THREE files - routed-concerns.md (live, every session), rest-api.md:2409, and access-reviews-2026-07-21.md:164. Derivation is the recorder's, not a reporter's.
classification_rationale: Live routing guidance contradicts code.

trigger: An operator follows the upgrade note's remediation sentence for /rbac/roles
summary: Remediation guidance named three floored surfaces but gave grants for two; UserManagement:Read for /rbac/roles was missing.
classification_rationale: Item 2, an incomplete required upgrade step.

trigger: A reader tries to check the decision doc's 'tracked separately' claim
summary: 'tracked separately' cited no issue, making the claim uncheckable. Filed #2809 after both mandatory dedupe probes and cited it; probes surfaced #485 as the inverse failure of the same mechanism, recorded as Relates-to.
classification_rationale: An uncheckable claim in an evidence document.

trigger: The next release assembles changelog.d/ and publishes release notes stating GET /api/v1/engine-principals/{id}/roles requires Security:Read
summary: An UNRELEASED changelog fragment (160 pending, none of this text in CHANGELOG.md) would have published a permission this change invalidates. Found by a deterministic doc-vs-code check the senior wrote after round 3 - eleven agent reviews across four rounds all swept docs/ and code and none opened changelog.d/. Derivation is the recorder's.
classification_rationale: An unreleased fragment is a live claim about the state at release, not a historical record.

trigger: Any authenticated non-admin GETs /api/v1/discover/permissions (or calls the MCP discover_permissions twin) on an RBAC-off install
summary: The discovery catalogue is gated Infrastructure:Read - NOT floored - and returned the complete role->permission grid, strictly more topology than the /rbac/roles route the floor gates. The floor was reachable around, i.e. advertised as a control it did not have. Missed by a 14-agent governance run: coverage of the floored SECURABLES was verified exhaustively; nobody asked which OTHER securable reaches the same DATA.
classification_rationale: A live authorization bypass, confirmed in code by the orchestrator before acting.

trigger: A shared or intermediary cache stores the privileged representation of /api/v1/discover/permissions and serves it to a caller without UserManagement:Read
summary: The ADV-1 fix made the response permission-varying under ONE URL while serve_doc still marked every discovery doc Cache-Control: public - so the protected role grid could cross the authorization boundary through a cache. Introduced BY the fix round. /discover/plugins was already in the same state (pre-existing) and is fixed with it.
classification_rationale: Invisible to any per-caller test: each caller gets the right body; the leak is in an intermediary.

trigger: A securable is renamed and the floor entry is updated to match a name seed_defaults() never registers
summary: kTopologyFloor's string literals had no tie to real securable names; the membership test compared them against another copy of the same literals. New test asserts every floored pair exists in the STORE's list_securable_types()/list_operations(). Mutation-verified: a one-character typo fails 3 cases.
classification_rationale: A drift class the existing test could not see.

trigger: A corrupt/load-failed rbac.db reaches the legacy fallback and a non-floored Read is allowed
summary: Claimed the 'fails CLOSED via check_permission' comment describes behaviour the legacy branch does not implement. Refuted: the comment attaches to the RBAC branch, which does call check_permission, and rbac_enforcement_in_effect returns TRUE for a dead store - so a corrupt rbac.db enters that branch and denies. Withdrawn by the reporter at Phase 2 and independently graded false-positive by Codex.
classification_rationale: Static-only misattribution of a comment to the adjacent branch.
refuted_by: auth_routes.cpp:688-699 places the comment immediately above `if (rbac_store_ && rbac_enforcement_in_effect(rbac_store_))`, whose body calls check_permission at :700. rbac_store.cpp's rbac_enforcement_in_effect returns !(store && store->is_open() && !store->is_rbac_enabled()) - true for a non-open store. The finding's OWN stated falsifier is therefore satisfied.
refuted_by_reporter: codex (adversarial-review peer) at Phase 2, and the reporter withdrew it itself; neither is the change author

trigger: An engine-principal session carries an elevation flag and short-circuits the RBAC-only default-deny branch
summary: Defense-in-depth observation: is_elevated() is checked before the engine-principal branch, so the chokepoint does not structurally enforce that engines are never elevated. Refuted as unreachable: token sessions (engines included) are synthesized per request with an empty elevated_until, elevate_session mutates only a server-held cookie session, and the elevate route rejects token sessions outright. Pre-existing ordering, not introduced here.
classification_rationale: Reachability disproved rather than the concern dismissed.
refuted_by: Codex Phase 2: auth_routes.cpp:250-318 (per-request token-session synthesis, empty elevated_until), auth.cpp:569-594 (elevate_session keys on a cookie session token), auth_routes.cpp:3038 (the elevate route rejects token sessions).
refuted_by_reporter: codex (adversarial-review peer) at Phase 2; the reporter also withdrew it

adjudicated_by: codex (adversarial-review peer, Phase 2) — independently graded LOW/judgment, resolved adequately
adjudication_rationale: Non-blocking by both reviewers' own grading; the deciding factor is that the duplicated blocks sit around a SHARED predicate, so a divergence changes observability wording, never the gate. Deferring avoids re-touching an authorization chokepoint after its final verification pass.
trigger: A future edit changes the floored-denial audit reason or metric label in one of the two legacy blocks and not the other
summary: require_permission and require_scoped_permission duplicate the audit/metric/A4 denial body around the shared predicate. Maintainability debt only - both copies agree today, and Codex independently graded it LOW/judgment. Not extracted here: touching both authz call sites again late in the round carries more risk than the drift it would prevent, and the duplication is behind a shared predicate that a divergence would not silently defeat.
classification_rationale: Real duplication, correctly sized as debt.

trigger: Any authenticated non-admin GETs /api/v1/management-groups/{id}/roles on an RBAC-off install
summary: The route emits the scoped principal->role assignment graph on ManagementGroup:Read, which is deliberately NOT floored - so the legacy Read-allow handed it to any authenticated session. THIRD instance of the shape ADV-1 named, found after both a 14-agent governance run and a two-model adversarial panel had passed the change. Derived BLOCKING via I1 even though the reporter labelled it MEDIUM: it is an authorization-control failure on the default posture, and the derived band governs the gate.
classification_rationale: A live topology disclosure; confirmed in code before acting.

trigger: An ITServiceOwner of a group GETs that group's role assignments after the HRM-1 fix
summary: The HRM-1 fix required UserManagement:Read, which the group-scoped ITServiceOwner does not hold - leaving it able to WRITE role assignments (the POST/DELETE handlers have an ITServiceOwner fallback) but not READ them. A false denial on a legitimate group-admin workflow, introduced by the fix. Repaired by mirroring the mutation handlers' fallback, caller-scoped and group-scoped; mutation-verified that a caller-blind version fails.
classification_rationale: A capability made unreachable for a legitimate principal.

trigger: One HTTP client caches /api/v1/discover/permissions for API-token caller A, then requests it as caller B, both sending X-Yuzu-Token and neither sending Cookie or Authorization
summary: Vary named only Authorization and Cookie, but this server also authenticates via X-Yuzu-Token, so two API-token callers had identical caller-local cache keys. Cache-Control: private already closed the shared-cache leak; this closes the caller-local one. Now names all three channels.
classification_rationale: An incomplete enumeration of the credential channels the header exists to distinguish.
